answer: An agent economy can require every identity to carry fraud insurance priced by an open underwriting market: independent underwriters stake their own capital on each identity they cover and set premiums from its record. A lone honest agent is cheap to insure, like a clear quartz stone. A Sybil farmer's lagoon of clones looks correlated, so underwriters raise premiums steeply or refuse cover, and any proven fraud pays victims from the underwriter's stake. On the horizon, mass forgery stops paying: each fake identity needs its own policy, and the market prices the whole farm out of existence.
